question.prompt: The weight of \(\frac{1}{3}\) of a large pizza together with \(3\frac{1}{2}\) cups of orange slices is the same as the weight of \(\frac{3}{4}\) of a large pizza together with \(\frac{1}{2}\) cup of orange slices. A cup of orange slices weighs \(\frac{1}{4}\) of a pound. What is the weight, in pounds, of a large pizza?

solutions.title: Compare the extra amounts
solutions.explanation:
Removing the same amounts from the two equal-weight combinations leaves equal weights. Remove \(\frac13\) of a pizza and \(\frac12\) cup of orange slices from each combination.

The first combination then has
\[
3\frac12-\frac12=3\text{ cups of orange slices},
\]
while the second has
\[
\frac34-\frac13=\frac9{12}-\frac4{12}=\frac5{12}
\]
of a pizza. Thus \(\frac5{12}\) of the pizza weighs as much as \(3\) cups of orange slices, which weigh
\[
3\cdot\frac14=\frac34\text{ pound}.
\]
To find the weight of the whole pizza, divide this weight by the fraction of the pizza it represents:
\[
\frac34\div\frac5{12}
=\frac34\cdot\frac{12}{5}
=\frac95
=\boxed{1\frac45}\text{ pounds},
\]
choice A.
